title: Other Chicago bands and how Chicago players took to New Orleans style
summary: The Hamfats never played an engagement together outside recording. Chicago musicians liked New Orleans style but played fast, arranged music.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, you played... Were the Hamfats the only band you played with when you were in Chicago?

Oh, no, I played with different other, you know, makeup bands. It's like you go on a gig, this musician at high, you know, different... But strange as it may seem, the Harlem Hamfats, we've never played an engagement together outside of recording.
How did the Chicago musicians at that time adapt themselves to playing with the New Orleans musicians in a New Orleans style? Did they take them long to learn or what?

No, it didn't take them long to learn. They liked the New Orleans style very much. But at that time, I don't know what... Call it swing or... I wouldn't know how to describe it as Chicago style. They'd play mostly fast, jumbled up, mixed up music. A lot of special arrangements.
Do you remember the names of any other band you played with in Chicago besides the Hamfats?
Well, just like I say, it's a different get-up band, you know, organized bands.
